sections.title: Why Master Instructors Need Assessment Design Skill
learningObjectives: Understand why this skill matters beyond simply administering existing assessments
Recognize that a Master Instructor judges whether assessments measure what they are meant to measure
sections.content: A Master Instructor doesn't just deliver existing assessments - they evaluate whether assessments are actually measuring what they're meant to measure, and may need to adapt or create assessment components for new content or new instructor candidates. This module builds that evaluative skill directly.

sections.title: What Makes an Assessment Valid
learningObjectives: Understand the concept of assessment validity
Recognize common ways an assessment can fail to measure what it intends to
sections.content: A valid assessment actually measures the competency it claims to measure - a common failure mode is an assessment that tests recall of facts when the real goal is practical competency, or vice versa. This curriculum's own two-part structure (written plus practical, from L2 onward) exists specifically to address this: written alone can't validate hands-on skill, and practical alone doesn't confirm conceptual understanding.

keyTerms.note: Whether an assessment actually measures the competency it is intended to measure, rather than a proxy for it.

video.title: A valid assessment in 30 seconds
video.transcript: What makes an assessment valid? It measures the competency it claims to measure. Failure mode: testing recall when you need skill. Or the reverse: testing skill when recall is the goal. Written alone cannot validate hands-on skill. Practical alone does not confirm understanding. So this curriculum pairs both, from L2 up.

sections.title: Setting an Appropriate Passing Threshold
learningObjectives: Understand the considerations behind setting a passing threshold
Recognize this curriculum's own threshold as a worked example
sections.content: A passing threshold should reflect genuine minimum competency for the role, not be set arbitrarily high (creating unnecessary failure and frustration) or low (certifying people who aren't actually ready). The module checks in this curriculum use a 60% passing threshold - a concrete example of this principle in practice, worth examining rather than just copying by default.

keyTerms.note: The minimum score or standard a candidate must reach to pass.

sections.title: Designing Rubrics for Practical Assessment
learningObjectives: Understand the purpose of a rubric in practical/performance assessment
Recognize what makes a rubric usable and consistent across evaluators
sections.content: A rubric breaks a practical assessment into specific, observable criteria - rather than relying on an evaluator's unstructured overall impression. This matters especially when multiple instructors evaluate different candidates: a well-designed rubric produces consistent results regardless of which qualified instructor is doing the evaluating.

keyTerms.note: A set of specific, observable criteria used to judge a practical assessment consistently.

sections.title: Writing Effective Assessment Questions
learningObjectives: Understand principles for writing clear, fair assessment questions
Recognize common pitfalls in question design
sections.content: Effective questions test one concept clearly, avoid ambiguous wording that could support multiple correct interpretations, and include plausible wrong answers rather than obviously incorrect ones that make the right answer trivial to guess. This mirrors the quiz design used throughout this curriculum - each question tied directly to something actually taught, with feedback explaining why the correct answer is correct.

sections.title: Reviewing and Revising Assessments Over Time
learningObjectives: Understand why assessments need periodic review
Recognize signals that an assessment needs revision
sections.content: An assessment that was well-designed initially can drift out of alignment with content over time, especially as modules get revised. Signals worth watching for include unusually high failure rates on a specific question (possibly indicating unclear wording rather than genuine difficulty) or feedback from learners pointing to ambiguity.

questions.question: Beyond delivering assessments, what else is a Master Instructor responsible for?
options: Setting the passing mark for every level of the curriculum
Judging whether assessments measure the intended competency, and adapting them
Marking every learner's written paper personally before results go out to them
questions.feedback: Correct. A Master Instructor evaluates whether assessments measure what they should, and adapts them as needed.

questions.question: What is assessment validity?
options: Whether it measures the competency it claims to measure
Whether an assessment can be completed in the time scheduled
How consistently different evaluators arrive at the same score
questions.feedback: Correct. Validity concerns whether the assessment genuinely measures the intended competency.

questions.question: Why does this curriculum use a two-part (written + practical) assessment structure from L2 onward?
options: Regulators require every industrial certificate to include both a written and a practical part
It reduces the time evaluators spend marking each candidate
Written alone cannot validate hands-on skill, and practical alone misses understanding
questions.feedback: Correct. Combining both assessment types addresses the limitation of relying on either alone.

questions.question: Two qualified instructors watch the same candidate and reach different results. Which change addresses this most directly?
options: Break the assessment into specific, observable criteria
Add a written test before the practical
questions.feedback: Correct. A rubric of specific, observable criteria supports consistent evaluation regardless of which instructor conducts it.

questions.question: One question in a module check fails far more often than the others. What should you check first?
options: Whether the pass mark for the check should be lowered
Whether its wording is clear and still matches what the module teaches
Whether the question should be removed so results are comparable
questions.feedback: Correct. A high failure rate on one question may mean unclear wording, not hard content. It is a signal worth investigating for assessment quality issues.
